records.table: A Pennsylvania rye family that went into business in 1810 gave Old Overholt its name, but Old Overholt Straight Rye Whiskey is made in Kentucky by Beam, four years old at 86 proof. Pepper and dark fruit make it a spicy rye to stir into a Manhattan.
records.story: The Overholt family farmed and distilled rye at West Overton, in Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania, from the early 1800s, and the brand dates itself to 1810, when Abraham Overholt (died 1870) took charge of the family still and made it a business. From 1854 the family built a second, larger distillery at Broad Ford. Abraham's grandson Henry Clay Frick (1849 to 1919), the industrialist born at West Overton, took control in 1881. The West Overton distillery never reopened after Prohibition, but the firm held a federal permit to sell its whiskey as medicine. In 1932 the firm was sold to National Distillers, which closed the Broad Ford still house in 1951, and the whiskey moved from distillery to distillery. In 1987 the James B. Beam Distilling Co. bought the brand with the other National Distillers labels, and Beam makes it in Kentucky. In 2020 the bottle rose from 80 to 86 proof without chill filtering, and in 2022 it gained a fourth year. The name on the label carries the Monongahela story to the bar, though the whiskey in the bottle is Kentucky rye.

records.table: Sagamore Spirit is the Baltimore distillery that set out to bring back Maryland rye, and Sagamore Spirit Signature Rye Whiskey marries a high-rye and a low-rye whiskey, cut to 83 proof with spring water from Sagamore Farm. Vanilla and honey lead, with a gentle pepper behind.
records.story: Sagamore Spirit takes its name from Sagamore Farm, a horse farm in Baltimore County, Maryland, whose limestone spring water brings the whiskey to strength, trucked 22 miles to the distillery, by the house's account. The founders set out to revive Maryland rye, a style the state had lost with Prohibition and one often described as softer than the Pennsylvania kind. While their own distillery was planned, they had two rye recipes distilled for them in Indiana, one high in rye and one lower, aged apart and then married and proofed in Maryland: that marriage became the Signature, at 83 proof. The distillery opened in April 2017 on the Port Covington waterfront in Baltimore, around a copper column still some forty feet tall. Its own Maryland spirit reached the bottle in stages, and in May 2024 the house launched Sagamore Small Batch Rye Whiskey, its first rye made wholly in Maryland, at 93 proof. The Signature is what put the Maryland rye name back in front of guests, and beside Small Batch it tells the house's story in two bottles.

records.table: In Pittsburgh's Strip District, Wigle pot distils Wigle Reserve Pennsylvania Straight Rye Whiskey from regional rye, wheat and malted barley, under the name of a Whiskey Rebellion rebel. It gives cinnamon, pepper and caramel, Monongahela rye made in the city again.
records.story: Western Pennsylvania made rye for close to two centuries, as the house tells it, and the style took the name of the Monongahela valley. In 1791 Congress taxed whiskey, and the farmers and distillers of the region rose against the excise. The distillery's name recalls one of them, a man named Wigle who attacked a federal excise officer, was convicted of treason and condemned to hang, and was pardoned by George Washington (1732 to 1799) in November 1795. A Pittsburgh family opened Wigle to the public in the Strip District in March 2012, and it is generally counted the city's first distillery since Prohibition. From the start it milled, fermented and pot distilled regional grain itself, and its ryes carry wheat and malted barley beside the rye, with no corn. In 2022 the founding family agreed to sell Wigle and its sister cidery to Pittsburgh Spirits. Pour it to show a guest the western Pennsylvania rye tradition as it tastes when Pittsburgh makes it once more, from grain grown in the region.

records.story: Two friends set up Mountain Laurel Spirits in Bristol, Pennsylvania, on the Delaware above Philadelphia, and began distilling there in 2011, to make rye in the Pennsylvania manner again. One of them had grown up around rye at his family's bar, and the whiskey is named for his father, who wore fedora hats and served rye at the family's tavern. The recipe follows the old Monongahela pattern of rye and malt with no corn: 80 per cent rye, 15 malted barley and 5 malted rye, fermented for about a week and distilled twice on a pot still with a side column. The classic rests at least six months in new charred quarter casks, small barrels that give the young spirit its oak quickly, and it was in bottle by 2012, at 90 proof. Larger barrels followed for straight and bonded ryes. Poured young, a rye of rye and malt alone tastes like this: floral, spicy and dry, a different animal from the corn-rounded ryes of Kentucky.

records.story: Washington County, south of Pittsburgh, was the farm country of the Whiskey Rebellion, where in 1794 protesters against the federal excise on whiskey raised liberty poles as their banner. A family founded Liberty Pole Spirits in the town of Washington in July 2016, naming it for those poles and distilling small batches of whiskey downtown. In July 2023 Mingo Creek Craft Distillers, the company behind the label, opened a larger campus in North Strabane, where a liberty pole had been raised in place of a groundbreaking, and moved all its work there. In May 2024 it released Old Monongahela Full Proof Rye, built on the old regional pattern: a mash high in rye, with malted rye, wheat and malted barley and not a kernel of corn, sweet mashed, batch distilled and filled at a low barrel entry proof of 108, then bottled at that same strength. Its label carries the style's own name, and the bottle shows a guest what Monongahela rye meant before the corn of Kentucky's ryes became the habit.

cards.prompt: What does Full Proof mean on Old Monongahela Full Proof Rye?
cards.answer: It is bottled at 108 proof, the proof at which it went into the barrel.

cards.prompt: What were the liberty poles that Liberty Pole Spirits is named for?
cards.answer: Poles raised by Whiskey Rebellion protesters in 1794 against the federal whiskey excise.

quiz.q: At what proof is Old Monongahela Full Proof Rye bottled?
quiz.explain: It goes into the barrel at 108 and is bottled at that same proof; 125 is the legal ceiling for barrel entry, not this whiskey's strength.

quiz.q: In which year did Whiskey Rebellion protesters raise the liberty poles that name Liberty Pole Spirits?
quiz.explain: The poles went up in the Whiskey Rebellion of 1794; 1776 is the year of independence, before the federal whiskey excise of 1791.

report: The plan's note asked the author to choose between Old Monongahela and the 92 proof straight rye: the record keeps Old Monongahela, which the house calls its Monongahela style rye and which puts the style's name on the label; the 92 proof Rye Whiskey stands under others. Its proof should not move between batches, since the house bottles at the barrel entry proof of 108.
Age is left out: one shop gives three and a half to four and a half years for batch D24, and the house gives none.
The release of May 2024 stands in Craft Spirits Magazine and a second trade post of 9 May 2024; Breaking Bourbon gives July 2024 as a release date, which may be wider distribution.

The founding of July 2016 and the 2023 move to North Strabane stand in Whisky Advocate, the Observer-Reporter and Visit Washington County; whether pot stills were used at the first downtown site rests on the house's description of small batch pot distilled whiskey.
Left out for want of a source: where the rye is grown (one review says Pennsylvania), the proof off the still (about 130 in one account), and the Whiskey Rebellion story behind the name Mingo Creek.
Not a benchmark pick and a house a guest may not know; it stays because it is the one label of the five that prints the style's own name.

story: pot stills at the downtown site is cut, since the two pot stills are reported at the North Strabane campus; the move is dated July 2023 (grand opening of 15 July 2023, WPXI and Visit Washington County), and the liberty pole was raised at the groundbreaking, before the campus opened.
